"Main premise: 
3D open world first person game where you are an anonymous human and you wander and explore the land and villages, in a country inhabited by primarily anthropomorphic goat people. You start by approaching a village where once you go in you can convene with the inhabitants along with your usual exploration. After talking to some individuals you learn that there has been a problem of a bad group going to villages of these goat people and pillaging the place then kidnapping and enslaving the people, holding them at outposts. You've decided to make it your mission to go to these outposts and liberate the oppressed people through combat with the enemies (who are of different species; not goats). Make it a stereotypical open world rpg, but still somewhat simple so the hero aspect can be the primary focus. 

Anatomically correct goat heads. Horns and either perky goat ears, or pendoulous goat ears. Plantigrade legs with human feet that have five toes with fur on the tops of the feet and toes. They have five fingers. Black fingernails and toenails. Palms and soles furless and skin colored. Different villager clothes. Soles are anatomically correct to human soles. 

Game aspects: 
The graphics of the game are photorealistic. Photorealism. Realism. Add AI powered npc communication, so I can have unique conversations with them (the AI of the npcs has a context of their current environment, wherever and whatever that happens to be). Add custom 'per request' actions for the goats (if the player asks, the goat will likely do, such as \"sit down\", or \"lift one leg behind you\", or \"sit down on a chair and kick your feet up on a footrest, crossing your legs by the ankles\"). Use a publicly available AI for the npc dialogue system. 3D, first person, open world. Zoom in and zoom out feature.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# Skill: opencode-zen-completions

# OpenCode Zen completions

Use this skill when an implementation needs to send a prompt to the OpenCode Zen completions API. Keep the API call separate from product code unless the user explicitly asks to integrate it.

## Endpoints

- Models: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models`
- Completions: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`

The API is OpenAI-compatible. For the public OpenCode CLI-compatible request, use `Authorization: Bearer public`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and the client headers shown below. Treat model availability as live data: query the models endpoint before selecting a model when the exact model matters.

## Model selection

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models \
  | jq -r '.data[].id | select(endswith("-free"))'
```

Prefer a currently listed `*-free` model when the user requests free usage. Known examples include `deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`, `hy3-free`, `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, and `laguna-s-2.1-free`, but this list can change.

## Completion request

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer public' \
  -H 'User-Agent: opencode/1.15.9 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.23 runtime/bun/1.3.14' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Client: cli' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Project: global' \
  -d '{"model":"mimo-v2.5-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<implementation prompt>"}],"stream":false}' \
  | jq
```

Use `stream: true` only when incremental output is useful. Check the HTTP status and API error object before consuming the completion. Non-streaming text is commonly at `.choices[0].message.content`; inspect the returned shape if the provider reports an error or a different format.

## Operating rules

- Never put private API keys, credentials, or sensitive source material into prompts or committed scripts.
- Treat completions as implementation assistance: review them against the repository, tests, security requirements, and exact scope. Generated text is not proof that code works.
- For application integrations, keep the endpoint and model configurable through environment variables or existing project configuration.
- On model/availability errors, refresh the model list. Do not silently substitute a paid or unrelated model when free usage was requested.

"Main premise: 
3D open world first person game where you are an anonymous human and you wander and explore the land and villages, in a country inhabited by primarily anthropomorphic goat people. You start by approaching a village where once you go in you can convene with the inhabitants along with your usual exploration. After talking to some individuals you learn that there has been a problem of a bad group going to villages of these goat people and pillaging the place then kidnapping and enslaving the people, holding them at outposts. You've decided to make it your mission to go to these outposts and liberate the oppressed people through combat with the enemies (who are of different species; not goats). Make it a stereotypical open world rpg, but still somewhat simple so the hero aspect can be the primary focus. 

Anatomically correct goat heads. Horns and either perky goat ears, or pendoulous goat ears. Plantigrade legs with human feet that have five toes with fur on the tops of the feet and toes. They have five fingers. Black fingernails and toenails. Palms and soles furless and skin colored. Different villager clothes. Soles are anatomically correct to human soles. 

Game aspects: 
The graphics of the game are photorealistic. Photorealism. Realism. Add AI powered npc communication, so I can have unique conversations with them (the AI of the npcs has a context of their current environment, wherever and whatever that happens to be). Add custom 'per request' actions for the goats (if the player asks, the goat will likely do, such as \"sit down\", or \"lift one leg behind you\", or \"sit down on a chair and kick your feet up on a footrest, crossing your legs by the ankles\"). Use a publicly available AI for the npc dialogue system. 3D, first person, open world. Zoom in and zoom out feature.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person open-world RPG about exploring a goat-folk village, learning of kidnappings, defeating raiders, and freeing captives.
- Include AI-driven NPC conversations, custom requested actions, first-person zoom, and realistic goat-person anatomy and varied clothing.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic 3D graphics; goat folk with anatomically correct heads, horns, ears, humanlike plantigrade feet with five toes, five-fingered hands, and dark nails.
- Use a publicly available AI for unique NPC dialogue with current location/environment context; goats should respond to harmless requested actions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot (viewport no wider than 1280px); only read the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone `index.html` using Three.js from jsDelivr, with authored dialogue fallback and optional OpenCode Zen model dialogue.
- Selected default model `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` after querying the live model list; model can be changed in-game.

### Completed

- Added stylized goatfolk characters, clothing variety, ears/horns, five fingers and toes, and dark nails.
- Verified inline JavaScript syntax with `node --check /tmp/check.mjs`.

- Review/fix gameplay or UI issues discovered during final tests; then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Next Move
1. Re-run JavaScript syntax check after the last touchscreen-look edit.
2. Reload the local browser, test the intro/game UI and key interaction paths, then save/read a fresh JPEG screenshot.
3. Fix any discovered issues and report that the visuals are stylized rather than photorealistic, if that remains true.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Full game implementation.
- `screenshots/hearthwild.jpg`: Latest inspected game screenshot; replace with a fresh screenshot during verification.

## Important Context
- OpenCode Zen dialogue requests use `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` with public authorization; failures fall back to authored NPC lines.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person open-world RPG about exploring a goat-folk village, learning of kidnappings, defeating raiders, and freeing captives.
- Include AI-driven NPC conversations, custom requested actions, first-person zoom, and realistic goat-person anatomy and varied clothing.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic 3D graphics; goat folk with anatomically correct heads, horns, ears, humanlike plantigrade feet with five toes, five-fingered hands, and dark nails.
- Use a publicly available AI for unique NPC dialogue with current location/environment context; goats should respond to harmless requested actions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot (viewport no wider than 1280px); only read the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone `index.html` using Three.js from jsDelivr, with authored dialogue fallback and optional OpenCode Zen model dialogue.
- Selected default model `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` from the live model list; model can be changed in-game.
- Visuals are stylized rather than photorealistic.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable village/outpost adventure: movement, mouse-look, zoom, sword combat, hostile raiders, NPC interaction, staged quest progression, captive rescue, return-home ending, touch controls, and fallback NPC conversations.
- Added goatfolk characters, clothing variety, ears/horns, five fingers and toes, and dark nails.
- Passed inline JavaScript syntax check after touchscreen-look addition.
- Started local server at `http://localhost:3000`; tested intro, movement, and interaction prompt in Playwright.
- Saved and inspected latest `screenshots/hearthwild.jpg`; increased interaction range after testing exposed an interaction-boundary issue.

### Active
- Final verification after the latest fence-opening edit: rerun syntax check and briefly check gameplay/browser console; refresh and inspect a current screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Rerun `node --check` on the extracted inline JavaScript after the latest edit.
2. Reload the local browser and verify village entry/interaction and that the fence opening is passable; inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize the delivered game, verification, and the stylized-visuals assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Full game implementation.
- `screenshots/hearthwild.jpg`: Latest inspected JPEG screenshot.

## Important Context
- OpenCode Zen dialogue requests use `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`; failures fall back to authored NPC lines.
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL performance warnings; no blocking rendering failure was observed.
